summary: lear 35 pressurization control failed. flt crew declared emer; apch and lndg completed uneventfully.

flight crew departing clt reports entering a runway change into the fmc prior to gate departure but forgetting to reenter the rnav departure which is runway dependent.  a track deviation occurs but no loss of separation.

air carrier dispatcher laments the lack of training when new procedures are implemented. he also believes that acars is an essential tool for communicating directly with the flight crew; which his company does not use.
pa28 pilot in the pattern at lom reports an nmac with a c310 entering on the left base with minimal communication.
flight crew flying emb jet exceeded 250 kt restriction under 10;000 ft.
a c172 violated the dca adiz because of a vor failure.
a b737-700 flight crew reported le flap transit light after takeoff that went out; only to reappear on arrival. they diverted to a nearby airport that had longer runways and landed without incident.
an md80 experienced atc com difficulty when an internal failure of the observer's audio panel made the observer's oxygen mask mike hot.
laf controller and a pilot reported a near midair collision between two small aircraft; in which one was late making a mandatory report; due to frequency congestion.
b767 flight crew experiences an intermittent stuck mic during descent; approach and missed approach before regaining communications and landing normally.
a crj200 flight crew shutdown the left engine and diverted to a nearby airport due to fluctuating low oil pressure.
aa5 pilot at 8500 feet reported being informed by zab that his mode c showed 9000 feet. the reporter believed that the problem was with zab.
cl-604 captain reported a track deviation occurred when the fms deviated from the programmed route for unknown reasons.
emb-505 flight crew reported executing an uneventful precautionary diversion due to failure of secondary ecs system.
a c320 on lndg had the lndg gear collapse incurring damage to the gear doors; props and engs. cause of gear collapse unknown.
a b757 first officer reported auto pilot and hydraulic power failure on initial climb and return to departure airport.
tower controllers reported a runway incursion with a departure and a vehicle.
cessna 172 pilot reported an incident when excessive braking on landing resulted in two blown tires.
aa5 pilot reports encountering heavy turbulence at 5;000 ft while attempting to use nexrad to avoid the worst weather.
citation x captain reported a failure of the 'hydraulic system a' during climbout and a subsequent successful diversion and landing.
air carrier first officer reported there was a slight perceived bleed through using the papi of white on the red light and red on the white lights; meaning the colors washed together.
pt-13 pilot reported loss of directional control after landing; resulting in wingtip contact with the ground; a runway excursion; and the aircraft ending up on its nose in the mud.
an air carrier crew descending into freeport at 7;000' climbed 500' in response to opposite direction vfr traffic on the airway when it generated a tcas ta. freeport atc has no radar.
ce560 departing teb experiences distraction from a stabilizer trim problem; and an altitude overshoot results.
emb-175 flight crew reported a passenger's portable battery overheated so the flight attendant placed the battery in a water container as per company procedure.
a320 flight crew reported a flap overspeed shortly after takeoff when they encountered a rapidly increasing headwind and wake turbulence from the preceding b757.

ce750 captain reports turning the wrong direction initially departing runway 16r at vny on the canoga 1 departure. both atc and the first officer detect the error and the turn is quickly reversed back to the right.

air carrier captain reported being notified by the company of a possible exposure to covid-19 through another crew member. the captain expressed concern that deadheading crew was notified before the on-duty crew and suggested that they should have been removed from duty sooner.
a b737-300 plt was distr during cockpit setup and failed to energize the ctr fuel tank pumps.
Crashed on approach, 7 miles north of the runway. Positioning for final approach by means of a non-standard procedure. Delayed detection of the VOR radial.
emb-145 first officer reported 'burning electrical' odor on flight deck which was also reported by flight attendants in the cabin. flight crew executed an uneventful diversion.
atc approach controller reported descending an aircraft below the mva resulting in the controller issuing an immediate turn to avoid the terrain.
maneuvering around clouds to remain in vmc; plt of c206 encounters another acft being vectored to the arc for an iap.

a b737 flight crew departing iah on the pitzz rnav sid as cleared to 'climb via' the sid 'except maintain 14;000 feet' as they approached the charted 4;000 initial top of climb.  the fms apparently dropped out of vnav mode as the new altitude was inserted in the alt alert window and the crew manually intervened as they approached jaylo climbing through the required 'at or below 5;000 feet.'
pct controller described a conflict event occurring after an aircraft was cleared for a visual approach on base; but failed to turn toward the airport to the correct runway.
vfr c172 on base leg for hef experienced conflict with tfc inbound to same complex rwy.
flight crew landing ce-560xls had near miss with small single engine aircraft taking off.
air carrier flight crew reported bird strike on takeoff climb. returned to departure airport and landed uneventfully.
student pilot reported a nmac while flying solo cross-country flight.

crj-700 flight crew reported forgetting to retard the thrust levers to climb after a flex takeoff due to distractions from a left pack temp caution and the captain having a pressing need to use the lavatory. the oversight was detected upon return to the flight deck. apparently no limits were exceeded.
c182 pilot reported taxi and lateral control difficulties on the first flight after an annual inspection due to a suspected failed or mis-calibrated steering bungee.
b737 first officer reported receiving a left irs drift alert along with increasing alerts and messages on the captains side resulted in a divert for a visual landing.
.air carrier captain reported first officer's window pane shattered during cruise. the flight diverted to an appropriate airport and landed safely.
vny tower controller reported that a local controller failed to notice that an aircraft was about to land on the wrong runway.
p210 plt downwind to lndg had to take evasive action to avoid another acft.

lark commander instructor pilot experienced a hard landing causing damage to the aircraft when his student attempted a simulated engine out landing from the traffic pattern and flared well above the runway. the instructor was unable to takeover in time to prevent a collapsed right main landing gear.
b737 flight crew reported an arrival to lax requiring multiple arrival changes; resulting in one crossing restriction that was missed.
c-172 pilot reported intermittent radio communication with atc.
air carrier ground personnel reported a wheelchair lithium battery was incorrectly transported in cargo compartment instead of aircraft cabin.
crj-700 flight crew rejected a takeoff due to a trim warning indication.
a b737-700 taxiing for tkof at rsw crossed the rwy 05 hold short line.

b737 flight crew reported an unstable approach at night with no vertical or ground guidance resulting in an unusual attitude situation. flight crew regained aircraft control with upset recovery procedures.
flt instructor plt described conflict while on crosswind at gfk with tfc entering pattern; indicating wx and or visibility contributed to the incident.
controller described an unanticipated turn by an ifr aircraft requiring numerous coordination efforts; later advised the aircraft experienced an electrical compass failure.

air carrier flight attendant reported a passenger misconduct and an unrelated issue of a passenger who allegedly checked a bag with lithium battery. the captain was notified of both issues with no additional information provided.
bonanza 35 pilot reported a nmac with another light aircraft in the pattern at mle airport.
crj captain reported that distraction and a runway change resulted in takeoff with an incorrect flap setting.
an instructor flying near the sdz vor at 3;300 feet took evasive action from a uav which fay tracon did not have on radar.

air carrier captain reported selecting an improper altimeter setting as received on the atis from atc; resulting in a low altitude alert while on an instrument approach in mountainous terrain. the crew leveled the aircraft then continued the approach; and after landing; atc updated the atis to the correct altimeter setting.

helicopter pilot reports being bumped on the main skid by a landing c140 as the helicopter is air taxied over the grass to parking. there is no damage to the helicopter and slight damage to the top of the aircraft's wing. the aircraft pilot lost control during the landing roll and departed the runway. the c140 pilot believes the rotor wash caused the loss of control.
zbw artcc enroute controller is off line when altitude is assigned to aircraft. adjacent facility calls up and queries center if aircraft is ifr or vfr.
uav pilot reported discovering after the fact that his aircraft overflew people at low altitude during a cinematography flight under part 107.
air carrier ground ramp personnel reported the flight crew failed to follow the chocked signal procedures which resulted in a rollback prior to securing the aircraft. the aircraft rolled 3-4 feet.
a b737 flt crew missed a san pdc lnsay two revision with a clrnc falcc direct sli. fms default to harbr intxn was accepted in error.
a b737-700 acft lh outboard aft flap incurred damaged during a bellcrank modification. titanium connecting rods were installed incorrectly and broke.
erj twice returns to departure airport due to pressurization problem.
ga pilot reported there is a crane less than a mile from the end of runway 18 at c47 airport; which is taller than what is noted in the notam.
a319 captain reported an excursion from assigned altitude due to a failed/malfunctioning fmgc2.

air carrier pilot reported during pre-flight they noticed the green hydraulic pump displayed on and hydraulic pressure was normal with engines not running. pilot refused to take aircraft in its current condition.
pilot reported a critical ground conflict after an opposite direction aircraft landed at the same time. the aircraft was not communicating on frequency due to a mechanical problem.

a flashlight battery overheated in luggage located in a b737-800's aft cargo compartment and caused the aft cargo fire warning to alert. the crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport where the hot luggage was found after an inspection.
a320 flight crew reported engine acceleration anomaly during takeoff roll resulting in a rejected takeoff.

air carrier first officer reported a traffic conflict on final approach when another aircraft on the runway did not start their takeoff roll when cleared for takeoff. atc issued a go-around clearance to the aircraft on final; then returned for another approach and landing.
emb175 flight crew reported momentary egpws warning on final approach.
b777 purser tripped over a curtain strap near the first class galley causing a head injury. the injury is severe enough to require a diversion back to the departure airport for medical treatment.
a medical helicopter pilot reported aborting a flight when he got a transmission chip light.
a319 first officer reports not noticing the speed limit of 250 knots until advised; on the accra1 departing mke; until notified by atc.
b737-700 captain reported significant uncommanded roll in both directions on initial climb related to jet blast from an aircraft on the ground performing an engine run for maintenance.
aventura avii pilot reported forgetting to use the landing checklist to prevent the gear up landing.

a very experienced ag cat pilot lost situational awareness during an agricultural spraying operation. he hit and broke several electrical power lines which he knew were there causing minimal aircraft damage.

zme controller reports of a star that goes to three runways. atis stated a specific runway in use; pilot sets up aircraft to land on that runway. unknown to atc pilot is going to a different runway than cleared and there is a 4;000 foot difference of altitudes between runway controller wanted and the runway the pilot was descending for.
b787 air carrier flight crew reported nose landing gear failed to retract after takeoff. returned to departure airport.
c172 pilot experiences radio failure on an ifr flight to rsw at night. knowing that rsw is imc the pilot elects to return to his departure airport in vmc.
interruption of a320 flt crew preparations by management plt contributes to errors of omission and commission on tkof.

b727 captain discovers a flap disagree light during approach with the flaps selected to 25 and indicating 20. with vref set at plus 10 for a crosswind the crew elects to continue to landing without referencing the qrh. the gpws flaps warning sounds several times prior to touch down.
c172 pilot reported loss of all electrical power during cruise and continued to land at destination airport where atc used light gun signals for landing clearance.

a320 flight attendants reported being unable to strap in as the aft aisle jumpseat 4-point harness had short lap belts; and suggested the aircraft be updated with the newer version that had longer straps.
bur tower controller reports of inadequate procedures for missed approach/go-around aircraft and the conflictions related to aircraft going missed approach/go-around.
an air carrier crew was cleared to cross a point at fl240 and after programming the fmc became distracted in conversation. consequently; they failed to set the mcp altitude and crossed the fix high.

an engine shop inspector reports inspection management violated an engine shop operations manual when they signed-up a pw-4000 engine for a final inspection; with the engine missing all fan blades; spinner and spinner cover.
md-11 captain reported a fuel truck did not follow proper procedures and interfered with his taxi on the ramp at lax.
an air carrier pilot reported a foreign air carrier does not include crew rest time during flights as flight time and is not complying with far's regarding crew rest after long overseas flights.
cma ctlr expressed concern regarding d-brite functionality and faa maint lack of access to repair same on mil fac during weekends.
air carrier captain reported experiencing an airspeed deviation and cited fatigue and lack of recent flying experience as contributing factors.
crj700 captain reports reports confusion while taxiing out for takeoff at bos.
far tracon facility scheduled a radar outage. the controllers were not advised or briefed about procedures to implement during the outage.
air carrier captain reported receiving a gpws alert during departure after turning too early.
c208 f/o reported an airborne conflict occurred when the flying pilot reduced his rate of climb approaching cruise altitude.
b737-800 pilot reported encountering severe turbulence on descent that resulted in injuries to a flight attendant and a passenger.
flight instructor reported their student lost control of the aircraft during landing resulting in a prop strike and left wingtip striking the surface.

challenger 300 captain experiences a flap fault during taxi out which the qrh indicates should operate normally during the short flight. the gear and flaps retract normally after takeoff but when the gear is extended for landing an amber l hyd press low; a gear disagree and a spoiler fail messages appear. a go-around is initiated and the gear is extended via alternate means; followed by a normal landing without nose wheel steering.
air carrier captain reported that being preoccupied helping an inexperienced first officer caused the flight to depart without proper documentation.
instructor pilot reported uim vor is notamed out of service.  however; the vor approaches for f51 and 3f9 which use uim vor as primary navigation are not notamed out of service/unusable.
air carrier flight attendant reported they were required to check their flight bag as cargo due to items containing lithium batteries.

crj200 first officer experiences a gear disagree caution message after takeoff.  qrh procedures are complied with and dispatch is contacted when the procedure is unsuccessful.  a second attempt at correcting the problem using the qrh procedure is also unsuccessful and the flight returns to the departure airport for an uneventful landing after burning down to landing weight.

a dispatcher working described being overloaded because of bad weather in the northeast. he was not given assistance by management even though other dispatchers were working less demanding flights in vfr conditions.

tower controller reported an aircraft lost control upon landing and veered off the runway into a ditch. the controller sent other aircraft around and coordinated with another controller to send other aircraft away from the runway.
oakland oceanic controller reported two aircraft at the same altitude; attempting to fix the problem but was unable due to communication failures.
ac69 plt experiences static system failure at fl250 after departing following a heavy rainstorm.
a dispatcher issuing a new maint release is asked by an md80 captain why the mel and placard was removed; but not repaired.
pilot reported their navigation database does not contain the fix cadre for the rockt1 sid from luk airport.
air carrier captain reported departing without proper takeoff data; citing high workload and career uncertainties related to covid-19 cutbacks as contributing.

a momentary erroneous right turn command as the fms transitioned from heading to lnav mode while flying the ruudy rnav sid from teb resulted in a premature turn to intercept the track to wentz. that distraction contributed to a small altitude deviation when the pilot flying failed to level at 1;500 ft msl as charted.

c206 pilot experiences a rough running engine just after takeoff on a very cold day and elects to return and land opposite direction on the departure runway. post flight discussions with an a&p mechanic reveal that high oil pressure may have produced the anomaly. the aircraft operates normally the next day.
corporate pilot reported hearing a significant amount of chatter on guard frequency that was not related to safety of flight.
la center controller reported an aircraft conflict likely due to pilot hypoxia.
recreational / hobbyist uas pilot reported losing visual line of sight of their uas and flying within an active tfr without authorization.
phl tracon controller reported an aircraft was not separated from an obstacle on departure; nor the mva; which reportedly is a frequent occurrence.
an air carrier aircraft departed iah runway 15r and took evasive action to a tcas ra 'descend descend' warning during a near miss with a small high wing aircraft in its departure path.
emb-145 captain reported they executed a rejected takeoff after receiving an e(2) rev disagree message. post flight inspection revealed the inhibit bolt on the exterior of the reverser was missing.

in vmc conditions; a b777 captain on approach to lhr runway 27r disengaged the autopilot after the loc activated then attempted a turned to a 360 heading instead of 271 to track the localizer. with autopilot off and while hand flying; the same anomaly occurred. after landing a fmc message rw ils error was displayed.
a pilot began the takeoff roll on sgs runway 16 after making the suggested ctaf communications; then aborted and exited the runway when another aircraft was seen taking off opposite direction.
a320 flight crew on final approach reported a heavy b787 turning short final above them. the flight crew received a ra to descend; and executed a go-around.

pilot reported not being able to receive clearance through pdc and requested verbal clearance from atc. pilot stated a portion of the clearance was not familiar to them and had difficulty getting atc to clarify it.
c172 in practice area near hsv arpt experienced conflict with c172 at 4500 ft after turning atc freq down to instruct student.
b737 captain reported that distraction and time pressure caused a departure with incorrect performance data.
ramp person reported a close encounter with an aircraft inbound to the same gate from which he was pushing an aircraft back for departure.
pa28 plt has near collision with pa38 during tkof roll at small unctled arpt.
c182 pilot reports conflict with another acft; under tower control; during visual approach.
b757 dispatcher reported a weight and balance miscommunication concerning fuel.

single engine pilot reported an electrical failure causing communication and navigation failures. the pilot and safety pilot used their efb devices to navigate to the airport. communication was reestablished on the ground by use of a handheld radio.
an air carrier pilot reported the approach they were issued had not been updated in the fmc database.
be58 pilot reports alt dev on the teb 5 departure; climbing to 1900 ft before correcting back to 1500 ft.
an a320 flt crew on descent into jfk descended below cleared alt when they were given a late rwy change.
air taxi first officer reported an aircraft attempted to taxi and park between them and another parked aircraft with inadequate clearance.
pilot reported missing signage for taxiways at avl airport resulted in deviation from taxi instructions.
flight crew reported a duct one over temperature on departure and the smell of smoke. flight crew returned to landing at departure airport.
crj-200 captain reported receiving two gpws terrain warnings on a day visual approach.
small aircraft pilot reported loss of directional control during landing rollout due to high crosswind gust resulting in a ground contact.

upon receiving a 'monitor radar display' aural warning while initiating the flare for landing (during atmospheric conditions consistent with potential predictive windshear alerts) the captain of a b737-700 opted to complete the landing rather than initiate a go-around.
vfr c172 pilot has a close encounter with a flight of three a10 thunderbolts between acy and miv.

a b737-700 stabilizer trim siezed during climb with stab out of trim light and speed trim fail lights illuminated but the crew could manually trim nose up after a slight nose down input. the qrh was completed and an emergency was declared for the landing.
an md80 experienced a landing gear problem and lost their weather radar; forcing a diversion with the landing gear extended.

crj200 flight crew experiences a l/wing anti-ice yellow caution cas message at 80 kts and rejects. the aircraft had failed an anti ice test earlier in the day but had then passed when thrust was increased per maintenance instructions.
a321 captain reported a go around after an uncommanded roll at 100 ft. agl and loss of an elac.
b757 flight crew reported a fumes event during descent and continued to a safe landing at destination.

a b717 captain reported an autothrottle malfunction on takeoff roll that included potential engine overspeed and then ground spoiler deployment. a rejected takeoff was performed; all systems reset with no faults noted; and a normal takeoff ensued.

azo ground controller experienced a loss of separation when clearing an airport vehicle across an active runway without required coordination; the reporter claiming a supervisors directive caused a distraction.

navion pilot reported an abrupt yaw just after takeoff when the engine cowl opened. the pilot immediately landed the aircraft on the takeoff runway; departed the runway surface and impacted runway edge lights.

b737-700 captain experienced an over speed during descent in vnav with the speed programed to .78/284 for no apparent reason. speed increased from .78 to .82 mach; without turning on the engine anti ice or a wind shift.
capt ignores late occurring tkof confign warning horn and continues tkof.
a b737-700 crew accepted a climb from fl360 to fl400 to be level in 2 1/2 minutes but when atc discovered that restriction would not be met vectored the aircraft off route.
air carrier captain reported fo steep approach angle initiated a terrain alert due to older technology limitations.
dispatcher reported aircraft lost communication radios and returned to departure airport.
air carrier captain reported a taxiway incursion due to expectation bias.
an air carrier pilot reported the crew would not have heard a taxi instruction to give way to another aircraft if they had not been monitoring a different  frequency than the one they were assigned.
air carrier dispatcher reported the aircraft returned to the gate to load a shipment of vaccine that was initially forgotten.

a commuter air carrier flight crew addressed fatigue issues related to continuous duty overnight scheduled assigned to reserves by releasing them to 'rest' early in the morning so as to make them legal to fly the sequence.
b737 flight crew experienced a tcas ra at 7;000 ft approaching svmi and took evasive action. approach control appeared unconcerned and issued a conditional descent to 5;000 ft.
a80 tracon controller reported an aircraft was 700 feet high at a crossing restriction of a new rnav arrival route.
On a delivery flight the aircraft struck a clound covered mountain at 4,300 ft. Crew did not follow the prescribed course.
captain reported loss of gps signal and ads-b fault.
a bae125-800 at fl320 encountered a strong updraft followed by a downdraft which forced the aircraft initially up to fl326 then down to fl310 before the crew recovered to fl320.
an a319 eng comes in contact with the jetway while the acft was under the direction of marshaller with 2 wing walkers.

b737-800 captain reported the flight attendants notified the flightdeck of an odor in the cabin during cruise. the flight crew requested priority handling to the departure airport where a safe landing was completed.
sfo tower controller reported a go-around due to wake turbulence.
an md-11 nose wheel steering began leaking on short final draining hydraulic system 1 fluid and causing a hyd-1 alert so the captain landed and had the aircraft towed to the ramp.

a line mechanic was informed he failed to notice during his a-check that fire extinguishing discharge nozzles were previously taped over in the forward cargo compartment of a b767-300 aircraft. the etops aircraft had been released months earlier from a heavy maintenance check at a contract maintenance repair station.
ce-560xl first officer reported difficulty dealing with a descend via clearance; in part because of crew errors; but also in part because of multiple atc clearance changes.
air carrier captain reported ummanifested hazmat was loaded.
c172 flight instructors reported atc tower failure to separate aircraft resulted in both taking evasive action and a nmac event.

the aircraft could not taxi from 'spot 7' at bos without starting the second engine and applying excessive power (after clearing area behind them). bos ground informed the crew that there is a 'divot at spot 7; you're not the first.'

e145 flight crew reported a hard landing with excessive pitch down moment of the aircraft and applied full back pressure which then created a rapid pitch up moment. the captain took control; completed the landing; then taxied off the runway; and reported the hard landing to maintenance.
flight instructor reported they thought another pilot or the fbo had filled the aircraft with fuel.  engine quit due to fuel starvation.
flight instructor with student reported aborting the takeoff when they received a call from another aircraft warning of an aircraft on the runway.
c177 pilot reported a loss of directional control early in the takeoff roll that resulted in a runway excursion.
flight crew reported inoperative pitch trim over 205 kts. and returned to the departure airport.
a b767-300 pilot reported his dangerous goods manifest was improperly filled out.
md88 captain reports engine failure during the first takeoff of the day. takeoff is rejected and flight returns to gate.
a b737 crew given an incorrect clrnc and squawk were misidentified by atc after dep. the com distraction caused the crew to fail fully retracting the flaps and to exceed the flap extend spd.

a b737 flight crew requested a clearance below rvsm airspace when their autopilot began an uncommanded descent and a short while later an uncommanded climb. an elevator servo was found to have malfunctioned.
an acr plt notes that mia pdc clrncs do not clrly specify that an lnav proc is part of the dep clrnc.

b737 flight crew was informed enroute that one of the flight attendants had become emotionally distraught for unknown reasons. she is allowed into the cockpit to calm down then returns to the cabin about eight minutes later. upon shutting down at the gate the flight attendant in question opens the 1r door with the slide armed and leaves the aircraft via the slide.
emb-xrj flight attendant reported a loss of pressurization resulted in an emergency descent to the destination airport.

an air carrier crew was clear off their arrival direct to the oak ils 30 mitoe waypoint for a night visual and while descending to 2;000 feet received nearly simultaneous egpws and atc terrain warning at about 2;500 feet. evasive action was taken.
sav tracon controller issued an incorrect frequency to an aircraft. the aircraft became nordo and proceeded into an area below the minimum vectoring altitude.
acr capt concerned that his fo had not been trained by the company to fly a canpa (constant angle non precision apch).

ga pilot reported a conflict during their final approach to pae airport when an aircraft was cleared to takeoff on same runway then stopped by tower; but not before aircraft had incurred the runway.  reporter was instructed to go-around. pilot reported atc training had been a contributing factor.
part 107 uas pilot reported they learned that uas flights they conducted at an rc field were not covered by the coa; as previously believed.
b737 captain reported initiating pushback without dg final documents onboard. documents were requested and delivered during pushback.

a319 captain reports loss of fuel flow indication on the right engine during climb. other fuel anomalies lead the crew to suspect a leak but the lack of fuel flow indication prevent the crew from preforming leak assessment procedures. the crew returned to their departure airport without incident.
ground crew reported company mechanics pushing back an aircraft without wing-walkers that came close to touching the reporter's aircraft.
a c310 pilot landed gear up when he failed to check for three green. landing gear circuit breaker had popped unnoticed earlier in the flight.

air carrier flight crew reported entering an active taxiway at ord without clearance after following instruction from ramp and looking at the charts. during cruise; the flight crew discovered that the airport diagram and terminal charts were different from one another; with the same taxiway having a different identifier between the two charts.

a c208b pilot reported tks fluid odor from the prop slinger entered the cockpit after takeoff.  the reporter preflight tested the system; but failed to close the fuselage left air vent. reporter noted that residual fluid drains for an extended period with tks system off.
a zob controller described a loss of separation where the application of visual separation was not completed according to legal requirements.
b757 captain reports a rejected takeoff when aircraft begins to veer right with full left rudder on a narrow runway. a second takeoff attempt is successful.
g650 pilot reported contact with an apparent interloper issuing bogus atc clearances on the afghanistan fir frequency.

a controller took handoffs on two departures off different airports on converging routes. although both aircraft were climbing to 17;000 feet; the controller was initially only in communication with one of the aircraft. he could not make contact with the aircraft he intended to keep climbing and waited too long to issue other aircraft instructions to ensure separation.
c150 owner observed wing damage due to impact by a skydiver who landed on the parked aircraft.

a md80 captain reported that on the same trip two aircraft had mechanical problems which maintenance had signed off but which were not actually repaired. the first was cabin fumes which forced a return to land followed by a flight in which the spoiler fault light illuminated after it had been signed off four previous times.

although their crew oxygen pressure indicated 2000 psi; a b737-300 flt crew had concerns about their oxygen masks not inflating all the way. the pressure transducer was faulty; and crew oxygen was actually at 'zero' pressure.
a321 pilot reported after documenting discrepancies into the aircraft logbook; the aircraft was taken out service due to corrosion and cracks on the rudder.
crj-200 flight crew reported performing a rejected takeoff due to flight control anomaly.
b737-800 captain reported experiencing unwanted fuel transfer from the center tank to the wing tanks; resulting in fuel being vented overboard.
a b757-200 in cruise at fl380 experienced loss of r hyd fluid. pumps off per qrh proc; fluid loss caused by 2 worn o-ring seals.
alt dev during the teb5 dep being flown by a rated corporate officer who had displaced one of his crew.
tower cic described a go-around event resulting from the local controller's questionable spacing judgment between an arrival and departing aircraft.
e145 flt crew experiences air/ground switch related anomalies after tkof. follow qrc procedures and divert.
an instructor pilot reported observing the student descend too low on the approach when atc issued a low altitude alert.
rsw tower controller in charge (cic) reported the tracon cic did not follow published procedures concerning changing active runways.

air carrier captain reported a loss of nosewheel control when entering the ramp due to icy surface conditions while taxiing to park at night at a non-towered airport. the captain could not maintain directional control and received a tow safely to the gate with a tug.

certified flight instructor with student pilot flying a mooney m20c reported that they had to reject the takeoff due to low rpms. on the second attempt they rejected the takeoff due to low fuel pressure.
air carrier flight attendant reported a premature cabin door opening after another fa gave the gate agent a thumbs up prior to verifying the doors were disarmed. escape slide did not deploy.

while flying vfr; a pa28 pilot notices that the generator has apparently failed and a turn is made to return to the departure airport. during descent airspeed is noted to be near the red line but slowing produces a mushy feeling in the flight controls. the airspeed indicator is ignored and the aircraft is successfully flown to a safe landing by feel alone.
c172 pilot reported a controlled flight towards terrain event shortly after takeoff due to a misconfigured elevator trim setting.
air carrier flight attendant reported a fume event while waiting to board passengers resulting in physiological symptoms.
an a320 fo inadvertently selected max auto brakes before lndg. the crew did not realize max braking was selected until it was applied during lndg.
crj-700 flight crew reported experiencing faulty gps signal to navigation displays. atc was informed and provided heading clearances.
student pilot reported during landing they lost directional control and initiated a go around. during the go around the aircraft came into contact with a runway edge light.

c172 flight instructor with student reported experiencing engine issues with the rpms dropping as low as 1000 and cycling back to 2000 several times. the instructor took over the controls and decided to return to the departure airport. reportedly; the cause of the engine issue was a bent push rod.
an a319 capt ordered the fo not to change an iad star in the fmc after atc issued a rte change. a track dev and crew conflict resulted.

capt of a b777 rpts large discrepancies between planned versus actual zero fuel wt which result in difficulties in accurately planning fuel for best balance between schedule integrity and fuel efficiency.
air carrier captain departing dia reported loss of gps signal.
b737 maintenance technician reported the replacement part was damaged.
dubai tower cleared a heavy jet for takeoff then at about 100 kts commanded a reject while directing an aircraft on final to go-around. the go-around passed 500 ft-1;000 ft overhead.
b737 flt crew reports cabin altitude warning at fl330 with cabin altitude exceeding 15000 feet before manual control of the cabin is regained. flight continues to destination at fl190.
zoa developmental ctlr experienced operror at fl340 with a dsnding and clbing acft caused by a missed incorrect readback error.
business jet captain laments new sop's that have been implemented without any formal training and only a written guide describing how the new procedures should be accomplished.
widebody transport captain reported the gps out indications on approach. captain reported continuing approach on radar vectors to a visual approach.
a b767 took off with the flight attendants unseated when the prepare for takeoff announcement was delivered via a hand held microphone later determined to be inoperative.
b777-200 first officer reported low hydraulic center fluid eicas which resulted in poor crm; incorrect data from dispatch; and vague checklist reference.
air carrier first officer discovers after landing that the prevailing visibility is 1/4 mile instead of 1 and 1/4 miles as was thought to be what was broadcast on the atis.
student pilot flying c-172 reported loss of aircraft control during touch and go with crosswind that resulted in a runway excursion.
saab340 was evacuated during taxi-out when a strong burning odor was detected by cabin crew. source of odor was a seldom-used; cabin-located supplemental air conditioner.

The captain's actions and his judgement in initiating a go-around manoeuver with insufficient runway remaining after a long touchdown.

cl-350 flight crew reported a yellow caution message 'pri stab trim fail' appeared indicating a failure of the primary stabilizer trim system. the crew elected to return to the departure airport.

ce-560xl captain expressed concern about what he feels is excessive horizontal stabilizer free play he has noticed in several ce-560xl aircraft during preflight.

reporter was assigned new altitude which they didn't want; and atc assigned higher altitude anyway.
lsa pilot reports forgetting to remove cowling plugs during preflight resulting in high cht shortly after takeoff. the anomaly is quickly detected and the aircraft is landed in the remaining runway.
an emb-175 flight attendant describes an engine failure on departure from her perspective; and the ensuing return to the departure airport.
bonanza 36 pilot reported momentary loss of aircraft control during landing resulting in wing tip ground contact.
after an apparently normal landing an emb-145's left tire was reported burning by ground personnel; the aircraft was evacuated with one knee injury.
zdc controller described an unsafe condition when weather factors and in-trail spacing requirements overloaded his/her sector; the reporter indicated tmu efforts were not effective.
b747-200 captain reported outboard flaps showed a split and did not fully extend on approach. possible stuck indicator freed itself on taxi in; allowing flaps to extend.
atr72 flt crew arrives at destination only to find out they flew the trip with the tail stand still installed.
flight attendant reported captain directed everyone to deplane during boarding due to a fume event.
air taxi pilot reported his confusion during an sea ils runway 16r approach.
air carrier first officer reported being routed through multiple ramp sectors before handoff to ground control.

flight instructor at pvu expressed concern regarding the atc service provided by the tower contract personnel; claiming some controllers are unsafe and current procedures are not conducive to instrument training.

a line mechanic reports a lack of clear procedures in their maintenance procedures manuals (mpm) of who is responsible for the tracking of borrowed/robbed/cannibalized parts used on their aircraft from other carriers. one of their b737 aircraft had been released with a 'borrowed' n1 gauge part from another carrier.
a veze nose gear collapsed on touchdown because the worm gear extension teeth were stripped.

b737 first officer reported that during climb a 'tru fail' (transformer/rectifier unit) light came on along with the master caution. all associated electrical systems failed.

a b737 captain reported on an unreliable fuel quantity gauge; which had a history of problems but was reportedly operating normally. he was unknowingly landing in a low fuel situation; until he received low fuel pressure indications on short final.
md-11 captain reported his airspeed indicator became unreliable; possibly due to pitot icing.
an sr22 departing las experienced temporary com failure.
e135 flt crew elected to continue tkof after hvy jet entered dep end of rwy.
zoa controller described a developing conflict event when one of two military aircraft operating as a flight elected to depart the assigned altitude.

air carrier pilot reported non-emergency flight related transmissions on guard frequency. reporter stated this resulted in interrupted communications; creating a safety of flight issue.
air carrier flight attendant reported an on going fume event during a two day trip with no resolution.
b737ng first officer reported new checklist procedures increased their workload while conducting a bleeds off takeoff from a busy airport.
md11 flt crew turned onto wrong txwy; blowing over barricades. commercial chart displayed assigned txwy in red; apparently indicating it should not be used.
c172 pilot reported a nmac on final at a non-towered airport; resulting in a go around.
b737-700 flight attendant reported a pressurization problem during descent that caused oxygen masks to deploy.
a320 captain reported the aircraft failed to initiate a proper level off  while on the jfund2 arrival to bos. captain stated this is a reoccuring type of event.
a dhc8-300 flight crew reported that during a crosswind landing; the first officer's yoke became disconnected from the captain's yoke as a large amount of aileron correction was added.

a320 first officer reported an inoperative airspeed indicator during the initial takeoff roll. the captain rejected the takeoff and no damage occurred.

customer service employee reported there is a lack of proper staffing in the lobby; which makes it difficult to follow cdc social distancing recommendations as passengers bunch up in groups while waiting in line.
two ga pilots reported a person parked a tractor on the runway to prevent a landing at a private airport.
first officer of a crj-200 reported an ra while descending towards destination and cited the large amount of ga aircraft in the area as a contributing factor.
air taxi pilot reported while descending on a visual approach they received terrain warning and low altitude alert from atc.
